claims.statement: runtime_ownership.py is the shared ownership contract: ROOT_ADAPTER_PATHS and COPILOT_SURFACE_PATHS are generated in consumers and mirrored into .claude/bootstrap-root for restoration, TRACKED_AUTHORING_PATHS (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) are preserved when tracked, and CONSUMER_STATE_PATHS under .claude are never used as equality targets or overwritten on refresh.

A skills/openwiki directory under .claude or .agents is ordinary bootstrap-generated content until OpenWiki's installer writes the marker file .openwiki-install.json inside it; is_third_party_skill_dir requires both the path shape and the marker.

The state-directory README files under plans, explorations, session_logs, and quality_reports are bootstrap-owned and regenerated on refresh even though their directories are consumer-owned, while every sibling file is left untouched.

The installer's --commit-copilot-surface mode decides whether the Copilot surface is committed to the outer repository or kept as a local mirror; the choice is persisted in .claude/bootstrap-ownership.env and reused on later refreshes.

In full mode, after mode detection and source selection, install_bootstrap.py's main runs a fixed sequence: validate roots, validate the .agents takeover, require a complete full source, resolve the Copilot surface mode, migrate pre-Git state, copy the generated tree, substitute names, mirror root adapters, merge .gitignore, chmod scripts, configure core.hooksPath, warn about tracked paths, and sync state.
validate_install_roots rejects overlapping source and target trees, and --allow-self permits exactly one overlap: the bootstrap repository refreshing its own overlay from its own dist/.

validate_agents_takeover compares the live .agents tree, the mirror under .claude/bootstrap-root/.agents, and the generated source with marker-claimed third-party bundles pruned by _agents_tree, and refuses with 'Refusing .agents takeover' when the tree cannot be proven generated.

copy_generated_tree preserves consumer state, tracked authoring adapters, and marker-claimed third-party skill directories, and removes bootstrap-owned files the new generation no longer produces, walking only .claude and the restorable root paths.
populate_bootstrap_root mirrors the root-level adapter files into .claude/bootstrap-root so the Git-backed .claude checkout carries them, skipping marker-claimed third-party bundles.

merge_gitignore writes or refreshes an idempotent block between '# BEGIN multi-agent bootstrap generated/private AI content' and its END marker, updating patterns in place and leaving text outside the markers untouched.

sync_state_after_install runs state-sync.sh to create the distinct 'bootstrap: install/update <timestamp>' nested commit, and migrate_pre_existing_state commits a pre-Git .claude with real content as 'migrate: import pre-git state' first.

update_consumers.py regenerates dist/ unless --skip-regen (a generator failure stops the batch before any target), runs install_bootstrap.py without --mode for each consumer while passing through --dry-run, --local-only, --allow-self, and the Copilot surface flags, records a non-directory target or a non-zero installer exit and continues, then prints one 'FAILED: <path> (exit <code>)' line per failure and exits 1; its success banner prints only when every target succeeded.

check_runtime.py fails on missing required runtime files, invalid plan frontmatter, runtime drift between installed files and their generated source (including installed files absent from the generated target), Context Mode dispatch problems, and unguarded array expansions in hook scripts, and otherwise prints 'PASS generated runtime wiring is present'.

Runtime drift checking exempts a marker-claimed third-party skill bundle under .claude or .agents in both the drift and the obsolete directions, and skips consumer state and the bootstrap-root mirror.
The installer sets core.hooksPath to .claude/hooks/git-hooks once at install time and skips with a warning when the target is not a Git repository.

detect_install_mode reads only the target: --mode sidecar refuses full evidence or a linked worktree, --mode full refuses sidecar evidence, no --mode refuses both kinds of evidence or team configuration only, and otherwise chooses by the evidence found, defaulting to a fresh full install.

With team configuration only and no untracked .claude directory, when the tracked paths include .devcontainer/state-sync.sh, the plain-install refusal says the target looks like a fresh clone of a full consumer and says to run bash .devcontainer/state-sync.sh setup first, or pass --mode full; next to an untracked .claude directory it instead offers only --mode full and says a sidecar overlay must not sit next to an existing per-clone .claude/ setup.

main picks the sidecar profile from --profile, else the existing manifest's recorded profile (read_sidecar_profile), else skills, and the source from --source when given, otherwise dist/multi-agent for full mode or dist/sidecar/<profile> (default_sidecar_source) for sidecar mode; full mode warns 'full install ignores --profile' and 'full install ignores --purge-state'; require_source_exists refuses a missing source; a sidecar target then gets validate_install_roots with allow_self=False and no --allow-self hint, one warning naming ignored full-only options, and install_sidecar(target, source, dry_run, profile), and no full-install step runs for it; a FileNotFoundError for the git executable during detection or uninstall ends the run with 'git not found on PATH: install Git or add it to PATH, then rerun.' instead of a traceback.

Before parsing arguments or running any Git command, the installer removes Git's repository-local environment variables (the GIT_REPO_LOCAL_ENV_VARS list) so an exported one can never point detection or a write at another repository.

Mode detection treats only a 'not a git repository' failure or a missing target folder as no evidence; any other Git failure, such as a dubious-ownership error, aborts detection with Git's message and a safe.directory remedy.

--uninstall never runs the mode table: _run_uninstall refuses --mode full, a target that is not a directory ('Refusing --uninstall: <target> is not a directory.'), and any full evidence, then warns once about ignored full-only options through warn_full_only_options_ignored(args, uninstall=True), which names --source, --local-only, --state-remote or AI_STATE_REMOTE, the Copilot surface flags, and --profile for uninstall, and --purge-state for a plain sidecar install; with no sidecar evidence it prints the preserved-copy folder's path when that folder holds anything and 'no sidecar found; nothing to do' with exit 0, except that a target Git does not recognize as a repository exits 1 with 'Refusing --uninstall: <target> is not a Git repository, so it cannot hold a sidecar overlay.'; otherwise it calls uninstall_sidecar(target, dry_run, purge_state).
In full mode, require_full_source_complete refuses a source without .claude/hooks/scripts/state-sync.sh after validate_install_roots and validate_agents_takeover and before any write.

warn_tracked_paths runs after most of the full install's writes and turns a GitDetectionError from tracked_generated_paths into the warning 'could not check for tracked generated paths: <error>' instead of stopping the install.

A tracked .gitignore is not team configuration: FULL_INSTALL_ROOT_PATHS holds only .claude, .devcontainer, and the restorable root adapter paths, so a repository that tracks only code and .gitignore gets the fresh full-install default instead of a refusal.

_full_install_evidence reads the outer index once before either modern evidence check, and when any entry of any mode (a file, a symlink, or a gitlink) sits at or under .claude, the target has no full evidence even if .claude/.git or the ownership file exists; only when neither modern marker fired does it check a real, untracked .claude for legacy evidence: at least two of five bootstrap hook scripts under .claude/hooks/scripts plus either a tracked .devcontainer/hf-ai-sync.py or .devcontainer/state-sync.sh, or a local .claude/scripts/verify.py.

_fresh_default_refusal runs only in the two no-evidence rows (no --mode, and --mode full without full evidence) and refuses, before any write, a target that is not its repository's top level, a linked worktree, a bare repository, or a .claude that is a regular file, each with a remedy.

--backup-state is a standalone installer action dispatched by main before --uninstall and mode detection to _run_backup_state, which refuses a non-directory target and otherwise returns backup_sidecar_state's result, whose shared sidecar preflight aborts a target that is not a Git repository; with --dry-run it only prints 'would back up ...' and writes nothing.

The installer's --profile option accepts skills or workflow, is used only in sidecar mode, and defaults to an existing manifest's recorded profile, else skills; --purge-state is read only with --uninstall and moves the state folder .ai-bootstrap into the preserved-copy folder instead of keeping it hidden in place.
update_consumers.py forwards no --profile or --source, so in a mixed batch each sidecar consumer is updated in the profile its manifest records while full consumers refresh normally.

The verifier's control-plane provenance requires each live root adapter to equal its mirror under .claude/bootstrap-root/, so an edit to a tracked root adapter makes verify.py report invalid control-plane provenance until install_bootstrap.py's populate_bootstrap_root refreshes the mirror.

The nested .claude/.gitignore and .gitattributes are listed in CONSUMER_STATE_PATHS, so a bootstrap refresh keeps both byte for byte instead of deleting them as obsolete owned files, and the runtime drift check reports no drift for either.
An existing workflow sidecar upgrades by adding the two onboard skill folders while preserving previous units and tracked team files; the skills-only profile has no onboard skill.
